themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked dramatically to 17 this week compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,300% increase (z-score: 23.33)—suggesting a coordinated poster campaign or enforcement gap in Ridgewood/Glendale that emerged THIS WEEK.
evidence: 17 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 23.33 indicates extremely rare statistical event
Spike is newest 311 anomaly, appearing only in current week data
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: canvass neighborhoods to photograph and map posting locations; interview residents about frequency and content
City enforcement angle: contact DSNY/311 to understand why enforcement lags; request posting complaint data to identify hotspots

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak This Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 7 THIS WEEK versus a 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 1,020% spike (z-score: 5.74)—indicating a sudden vandalism wave in the district.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 average weekly baseline
Emerged this week alongside illegal posting spike, suggesting possible coordinated activity or neighborhood blight acceleration
reporting_angles: Visual documentation: photograph graffiti locations, themes, and tags to identify gang/crew activity or copycat vandalism
Community impact: interview residents and business owners about sense of disorder; check if street cleaning or enforcement has been delayed

themes_detail.label: Damaged Street Signs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints rose to 9 THIS WEEK versus 2.4 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 279% increase (z-score: 7.73)—suggesting either a weather event, traffic incident wave, or maintenance backlog in the district.
evidence: 9 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 average weekly baseline
z-score of 7.73 indicates highly unusual spike
Coincides with graffiti and illegal posting surges, suggesting broader neighborhood infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Root cause investigation: check DOT maintenance schedules and weather data from this week; interview DOT about backlog of sign repairs
Safety angle: identify whether damaged signs (e.g., stop signs, street names) pose traffic or navigation hazards

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 18 last week versus 5.0 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 260% increase (z-score: 5.96)—indicating accelerating street infrastructure failures in the district.
evidence: 18 complaints last week vs. 5.0 average weekly baseline (260% increase)
z-score of 5.96 indicates strong statistical signal
Aligns with repeated community board budget requests for DEP sewer inspection and repair—suggests this is a persistent problem now escalating
reporting_angles: Impact story: find residents with damaged sidewalks, trip hazards, or basement flooding; tie to aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance
Policy angle: interview DEP about sewer inspection backlog in CD 405; cross-reference with community board budget requests to show this is a known, unresolved issue

themes_detail.label: Pigeon Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary pigeon condition complaints rose to 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—indicating either a seasonal bird population surge or emergence of a feeding/roosting hotspot in the district.
evidence: 4 unsanitary pigeon complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 average weekly baseline
Coincides with broader sanitation complaints (graffiti, illegal posting), suggesting neighborhood conditions attracting wildlife
reporting_angles: Source investigation: locate roosting areas (overpasses, abandoned buildings, food waste sites); identify if recent construction or demolition created new nesting habitat
Community health angle: interview DOHMH about pigeon-related disease vectors; check if complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods (e.g., near parks, commercial strips)
